page: Microsoft Azure D4as_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine within the DASv4 series, powered by the AMD EPYC 7763 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled at a base clock of 3.35 GHz. The CPU cache architecture features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of shared L3 cache, backed by support for AVX, AES-NI, VAES, and SHA instruction set extensions. Memory capacity is configured at 16.0 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and the virtual machine includes 34 GB of local SSD temporary storage.

Benchmark results show a split between single-threaded efficiency and parallel capacity. In stress-ng single-core execution, the processor scores 2707.07, positioning it in the top 25 percent of tested systems. Conversely, its multi-core stress-ng result of 5410.95 and Geekbench multi-core score of 3600.0 fall into the lower quartile, reflecting the limited physical core count of a 4-vCPU footprint. Decompression tests show average single-threaded bzip3 rates of 11.42 GB/sec but drop to the bottom 10 percent in multi-threaded decompression at 21.66 GB/sec. Memory subsystem bandwidth reaches 33.54 GB/sec for uncached large reads and 21.76 GB/sec for large writes, while PassMark memory performance remains mid-tier at 2312.97.

The D4as_v4 represents a balanced entry point for general computation, offering dedicated AMD cores and low-latency local storage without demanding high operational overhead. Tradeoffs include restricted total parallel throughput, lower memory bandwidth on uncached block operations, and absence of hardware GPU acceleration. It is well suited for mid-sized web serving, microservices, enterprise application middleware, development environments, and moderate transactional databases requiring consistent single-thread responsiveness.
description: Microsoft Azure D4as_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DASv4 family, equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 7763 processor clocked at 3.35 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture, the instance includes 16.0 GB of memory, 16 MB of L3 cache, and 34 GB of local SSD storage, while excluding dedicated GPUs. Synthetic benchmarks reveal strong single-core CPU throughput, reaching 2707.07 on stress-ng, alongside average single-threaded compression performance. However, due to its compact four-thread configuration, multi-core throughput and uncached memory bandwidth fall within the bottom quartile relative to larger enterprise hardware. As a result, the instance represents an efficient configuration for balanced, moderately concurrent tasks such as web application hosting, caching layers, containerized microservices, and general enterprise backend processing.
